Scene 03

Scene 03

Prisoner

Prisoner. Hey. Prisoner. I thought maybe you were dead.

Fox Mulder

How long have I been lying here?

Prisoner

Hours. I don't know. The first time is bad. Very bad.

Fox Mulder

They do this to you?

Prisoner

Yes. It becomes easier each time, until it kills you.

Fox Mulder

What did they do to me?

Prisoner

You have been exposed to the black cancer.

Fox Mulder

What cancer?

Prisoner

The cancer that lives in the rock.

Fox Mulder

Who are you?

Prisoner

I was a geologist. Quite well known in my field, actually, but now I am just a test subject.

Fox Mulder

You helped them find the rock?

Prisoner

I was there when they brought up the first fragments. This was before the mining, before we knew what lived in Tunguska rock.

Fox Mulder

How many men have died here?

Prisoner

Hundreds. Maybe more. The search for a cure goes slowly.

Fox Mulder

Is that what they say the tests are for, to find a cure?

Prisoner

No, no. They tell us nothing. We are left to guess or imagine the reasons for our torture. But what else could it be?

Fox Mulder

What happened to the man who was in the cell with me-- Krycek?

Prisoner

He is most likely dining with the men responsible for our torture. I heard laughter when they left your cell.

Fox Mulder

I'm not going to die.

Prisoner

No? Why not?

Fox Mulder

I have to live long enough to kill that man Krycek. Where did you get this?

Prisoner

I made it... To kill myself. It took me nearly two weeks. By then, I had lost the desire.

Fox Mulder

You'd rather suffer the torture?

Prisoner

It is wonderful, the persistence of life. That rock we found buried so deep in the earth, that anything could survive down there against all reason. No. They will have to kill me themselves.

Scene 07

OUTSIDE SCULLY’S APARTMENT

Walter Skinner

Agent Scully.

Dana Scully

Sir, what are you--

Walter Skinner

I've been trying to contact you for hours. The better part of the day.

Dana Scully

I'm sorry, sir. My cell phone was turned off.

Walter Skinner

You owe me some answers, agent Scully, answers I don't have to the questions I'm being asked about this missing diplomatic pouch. The pouch presumably being carried by the man who was pushed off my balcony... And whose connection to the felon I harbored in my house against all good sense, I'm going to have to explain to avoid perjuring myself before a senate subcommittee tomorrow, which, I might remind you, is a serious crime in itself, is it not, agent Scully?

Dana Scully

Yes, sir. Sir, if I might explain, the contents of that pouch, it contained some kind of a biohazardous organism... That is luckily being contained in a contamination laboratory at NASA goddard, which is where I've been all day, trying to determine its exact nature.

Walter Skinner

That pouch you intercepted, do you know what its intended destination was?

Dana Scully

No, sir, I don't.

Walter Skinner

Well, I do, agent Scully, because I bent some rules this morning when I couldn't find you, to find out who was to receive it.

Dana Scully

Who was it?

Walter Skinner

Dr. Bonita charne-sayre. Are you familiar with that name?

Dana Scully

Yes, sir, I am. She's a well-known physician, a virologist who's looked in on presidents. She's also an authority on variola viruses.

Walter Skinner

Variola?

Dana Scully

Smallpox. She's been a vocal proponent... Of eliminating the last remaining stores of the smallpox virus, destroying the only remaining vials in facilities... Here in atlanta and in the former soviet union.

Walter Skinner

Well, she was killed tonight.

Dana Scully

Killed?

Walter Skinner

A horse stepped on her throat in a riding accident in virginia.

Scene 14

SENATE SUBCOMMITTEE ON INTELLIGENCE AND TERRORISM

Dana Scully

I, Dana katherine Scully, swear to tell the truth, the whole truth...

[ gavel pounds ]

Dana Scully

And nothing but the truth, so help me, god. I would like to read from a prepared statement.

Chairman Romine

You may do so.

Dana Scully

"I left behind a career in medicine... "to become an FBI agent four years ago... "because I believed in this country, "because I wanted to uphold its laws, "to punish the guilty and to protect the innocent. "I still believe in this country, "but I believe that there are powerful men in this government who do not. "men who have no respect for the law and who flout it with impunity.

Chairman Romine

Uh, miss Scully--

Dana Scully

"I have come to the conclusion...

Chairman Romine

Agent Scully--

Dana Scully

That it is no longer possible--"

Chairman Romine

This is not a soapbox, ms. Scully. Your statement will be entered into the record.

Dana Scully

With all due respect, mr. Chairman, I would like to finish.

Chairman Romine

This is not why we are here today.

Dana Scully

Then why are we here, sir?

Senator Sorenson

Do you or do you not know the whereabouts of agent Mulder? Are you or are you not aware of agent Mulder's present location?

Dana Scully

I respectfully refuse to answer that question, sir, because--

Chairman Romine

Agent Scully, you cannot refuse to answer that question.

Dana Scully

Because I believe answering that question could endanger agent Mulder's life.

Chairman Romine

You don't seem to understand. Your response is not optional. You are an agent of the FBI.

Dana Scully

Then if I may please finish my statement. "that it is no longer possible for me to carry out my duties as an FBI agent."

Senator Sorenson

Are you tendering your resignation, agent Scully? Is that what you're trying to say?

Dana Scully

No, sir. What I am saying... Is that there is a culture of lawlessness... That has prevented me from doing my job, that the real target of this committee's investigation... Should be the men who are beyond prosecution and punishment, the men whose secret policies are behind the crimes that you are investigating.

Senator Sorenson

You have a legal obligation to answer the questions posed to you. Now, either you tell us what you know about agent Mulder's whereabouts, or you'll be held in contempt of Congress.
